plugin.sha512.title: SHA-512, SHA-384, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256
plugin.sha512.preset.sha-512-two-block: SHA-512 of the 112-byte example message (two blocks)
plugin.sha512.preset.sha-512-256-iv: IV generation: where the SHA-512/256 initial hash value comes from
plugin.sha512.preset.sha-512-224-iv: IV generation: where the SHA-512/224 initial hash value comes from
plugin.sha512.param.algorithmHint: All five share the 64-bit compression function with 80 rounds. SHA-384, SHA-512/224 and SHA-512/256 start from their own initial hash value and keep only the first 384, 224 or 256 bits. The SHA-512/t IV generator is not a hash function of its own: it is the FIPS 180-4 recipe that derives the initial hash value of SHA-512/t.
plugin.sha512.param.encodingHint: Text is hashed as its UTF-8 bytes. Hex lets you enter any bytes, two hex digits per byte.
plugin.sha512.param.inputHint: 0 to 128 bytes, which pad to at most two 128-byte blocks. The message may be empty.
plugin.sha512.param.detailHint: “Per round” shows every message schedule word and every one of the 80 rounds. “Per block” runs the whole compression function of a block in one step.
plugin.sha512.op.pad: Pad the message to whole blocks
plugin.sha512.op.init: Load the chaining value and the block
plugin.sha512.op.compress: Run all rounds of the block
plugin.sha512.op.feedForward: Add the working variables to H (feed-forward)
plugin.sha512.step.initial: {{algorithm}} turns the {{bytes}}-byte message into a {{bits}}-bit hash value. It pads the message to whole {{blockBits}}-bit blocks, then runs the compression function ({{rounds}} rounds) once per block, starting from the initial hash value H(0).
plugin.sha512.step.initialIvGeneration: The SHA-512/t IV generator (FIPS 180-4 §5.3.6) derives the initial hash value of SHA-512/t from its name: it hashes the {{bytes}}-byte ASCII text, e.g. “SHA-512/256”, with SHA-512 started from a modified initial hash value H(0)″, and keeps all {{bits}} bits. Same padding, same {{rounds}} rounds per {{blockBits}}-bit block; only the start value differs.
plugin.sha512.step.pad_one: Padding (FIPS 180-4 §5.1.2): after the {{bytes}} message bytes ({{bits}} bits) come the byte 80 (the bit 1 and seven zero bits), {{zeros}} zero bytes and the message length in bits as a {{lengthBits}}-bit number. The result is {{count}} block of {{blockBytes}} bytes.
plugin.sha512.step.pad_other: Padding (FIPS 180-4 §5.1.2): after the {{bytes}} message bytes ({{bits}} bits) come the byte 80 (the bit 1 and seven zero bits), {{zeros}} zero bytes and the message length in bits as a {{lengthBits}}-bit number. The result is {{count}} blocks of {{blockBytes}} bytes.
plugin.sha512.step.initFirst: H(0) is the {{algorithm}} initial hash value: {{h}}. The working variables a … h start as H(0), and W₀ … W₁₅ are the 16 words of block 1, read big-endian.
plugin.sha512.step.initFirstIvGeneration: H(0)″ is the SHA-512 initial hash value with every word XORed with {{mask}} (FIPS 180-4 §5.3.6): H(0)″ = H(0) ⊕ {{mask}}… = ({{base}}) ⊕ {{mask}}… = {{h}}. The new start value keeps SHA-512/t apart from SHA-512 itself. The working variables a … h start as H(0)″, and W₀ … W₁₅ are the 16 words of block 1, read big-endian.
plugin.sha512.step.init: Block {{n}} starts from the chaining value H({{prev}}) = {{h}}: a … h ← H({{prev}}), and W₀ … W₁₅ are the 16 words of block {{n}}.
plugin.sha512.step.schedule: W{{t}} = σ1(W{{t2}}) + W{{t7}} + σ0(W{{t15}}) + W{{t16}} = {{sigma1}} + {{w7}} + {{sigma0}} + {{w16}} = {{w}} (addition mod 2^{{wordBits}}). Each new word mixes four earlier words, so every message bit reaches many rounds.
plugin.sha512.step.round: Round {{t}}: T1 = h + Σ1(e) + Ch(e, f, g) + (K{{t}} + W{{t}}) = {{T1}} with K{{t}} + W{{t}} = {{kw}}, and T2 = Σ0(a) + Maj(a, b, c) = {{T2}} (mod 2^{{wordBits}}). The new a = T1 + T2 = {{a}}, the new e = d + T1 = {{e}}; b, c, d and f, g, h take the old values of a, b, c and e, f, g.
plugin.sha512.step.compress: Block {{n}}: the message schedule and all {{rounds}} rounds in one step. Afterwards a … h = {{vars}}.
plugin.sha512.step.feedForward: Feed-forward: H({{n}}) = H({{prev}}) + (a, …, h), word by word mod 2^{{wordBits}} = {{h}}. Adding the input back makes the compression function hard to invert.
plugin.sha512.step.output: The {{algorithm}} hash value is the final chaining value H({{n}}) itself, all {{bits}} bits: {{digest}}.
plugin.sha512.step.outputTruncated: The {{algorithm}} hash value is the final chaining value H({{n}}) truncated to its first {{bits}} bits: {{digest}}.
plugin.sha512.step.outputIvGeneration: The result is the final chaining value H({{n}}), all {{bits}} bits: {{digest}}. It is not a hash value but the initial hash value H(0) of the SHA-512/t named in the message: for “SHA-512/256” the eight words of FIPS 180-4 §5.3.6.2, for “SHA-512/224” those of §5.3.6.1.
plugin.sha512.formula.init: a … h ← H({{prev}}); W₀ … W₁₅ ← M({{n}})
plugin.sha512.formula.round: T1 = h + Σ1(e) + Ch(e, f, g) + K{{t}} + W{{t}}; T2 = Σ0(a) + Maj(a, b, c); a ← T1 + T2; e ← d + T1
plugin.sha512.error.algorithm: Unknown hash function “{{algorithm}}”: choose SHA-384, SHA-512, SHA-512/224, SHA-512/256 or the SHA-512/t IV generator.
plugin.sha512.error.encoding: Unknown input format “{{encoding}}”: choose text or hex.
plugin.sha512.error.inputLength: The message has {{length}} bytes; at most 128 bytes are allowed.
